title: openai-compat: support Responses API variants + seed/determinism + metadata passthrough
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Motivation: The OpenAI Responses API has multiple variants (responses/chat, responses/generation) and newer flags (seed/determinism, metadata passthrough) that customers expect to be supported by the OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR implements: 1) explicit mapping for Responses API variants to Redwood response shapes (chat/generation), 2) deterministic seed handling routed to samplers/decoders in the runtime, 3) full passthrough of user-provided top-level metadata fields into response.metadata and telemetry, and 4) streaming stability fixes to ensure deterministic event ordering for function/tool-calling and structured outputs.

What this changes: - API layer: adds responses_variant detection and versioned compatibility adapters (responses->chat/generation). - Request translation: maps OpenAI's seed and determinism flags to the runtime sampler config (seed applied when present; deterministic mode toggles fallback heuristics). - Metadata: any top-level metadata in the OpenAI request ("metadata", "user_metadata", etc.) is copied verbatim into the Response.metadata field and included in telemetry traces with PII-safe redaction policy. - Streaming: reworked stream event framing for tool/function calls to guarantee that "tool_call" events and subsequent "tool_result" events are emitted in order; added sequence numbers to internal stream events to aid clients that rehydrate streams. - Tests: added unit and integration tests for variant routing, seed determinism, metadata passthrough, and a flaky-stream regression test that previously surfaced in canary.

Checklist: - [x] Add variant routing and adapters - [x] Implement seed/determinism plumbing to runtime - [x] Preserve and sanitize metadata fields - [x] Add stream ordering guarantees and sequence numbering - [x] Update SDK response mapping tests (Python/TS) - [x] Add docs note (redwood-docs) linking compatibility behaviors - [x] Add rollout plan and feature flag for gradual enablement

Backward compatibility: Default behavior unchanged when no variant/seed/metadata provided. New behavior behind compatibility flag 'openai_responses_v2' that is enabled for existing accounts in staged rollout. See release_notes below for migration guidance.

Related: previously attempted compatibility PRs (pr-28567, pr-30245, pr-33642) implemented metadata passthrough and part of seed handling; this PR consolidates those pieces and adds robust streaming ordering for function/tool calls.

Testing and validation: Extensive unit tests added in redwood/openai_compat/, integration tests run against the perf-canary harness, and end-to-end smoke against redwood-quickstarts. Canary run showed 0.2% increase in median tail latency for small-requests but no impact on p99 for batched workloads.

Rollout: Feature-flag gated. Gradual rollout to 10% of traffic for two days, monitor structured-output diffs and function-calling failure rates, then expand if metrics stable.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the request->runtime seed mapping (openai_compat/seed_adapter.py) and stream framing changes (runtime/streaming/framing.py). The metadata sanitization policy is in security/metadata_redaction.py.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add responses variant detection and adapter
chore(runtime): expose deterministic seed hook to sampler API
fix(streaming): sequence-number stream frames for tool/function events
test(openai-compat): add unit tests for seed and metadata passthrough
docs: compatibility note and migration guidance
diff_snippets:
--- a/runtime/streaming/framing.py
+++ b/runtime/streaming/framing.py
@@ -10,6 +10,16 @@
 def _emit_event(conn, event):
-    conn.send(json.dumps(event))
+    # attach sequence number to ensure consumer ordering when rehydrating
+    event["seq"] = conn.next_seq()
+    conn.send(json.dumps(event))

--- a/redwood/openai_compat/seed_adapter.py
+++ b/redwood/openai_compat/seed_adapter.py
@@ -1,6 +1,21 @@
-def map_seed(req):
-    return {}
+def map_seed(req):
+    # OpenAI 'seed' -> runtime sampler.seed
+    seed = req.get("seed")
+    deterministic = req.get("deterministic") or req.get("temperature") == 0
+    cfg = {}
+    if seed is not None:
+        cfg["seed"] = int(seed)
+    if deterministic:
+        cfg["deterministic"] = True
+    return cfg

--- a/redwood/openai_compat/metadata_passthrough.py
+++ b/redwood/openai_compat/metadata_passthrough.py
@@ -1,4 +1,14 @@
+def passthrough_metadata(req):
+    # accept common metadata fields and copy them to response.metadata
+    fields = ["metadata", "user_metadata", "client_metadata"]
+    out = {}
+    for f in fields:
+        if f in req:
+            out[f] = sanitize_for_telemetry(req[f])
+    return out

--- a/redwood-docs/content/compatibility/openai_responses.md
+++ b/redwood-docs/content/compatibility/openai_responses.md
@@ -1,3 +1,14 @@
+## Responses API compatibility
+
+Redwood now supports the Responses API variants and the seed/determinism flags. Note: deterministic runs may reduce sampling variance and can change token-level outputs. See migration notes below.
review_comments: Priya Nair: This looks comprehensive. Can you add a unit test that asserts seq numbers increment across interleaved tool calls?
Jordan Lee: Added a flaky-stream regression test and a deterministic-seed integration test. See redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_openai_compat.py:TestSeedDeterminism
Ethan Brooks: Suggest tightening the redaction policy for 'user_metadata' to avoid accidental PII export. Left an inline comment on security/metadata_redaction.py
Jordan Lee: Updated redaction rules to drop fields named 'ssn' and 'credit_card' and to hash email-like fields.
ci_checks: perf-regression: pass (0.2% median latency bump on canary; within threshold)
release_notes: Added OpenAI Responses API variant compatibility, seed/determinism support, and metadata passthrough. Streaming frames now include sequence numbers to preserve ordering for function/tool calls. Opt-in via feature flag 'openai_responses_v2' with staged rollout. See redwood-docs compatibility page for migration guidance.
migration_guidance: Enable the feature flag in Console -> Feature Flags. If you rely on token-level determinism, set seed and deterministic=true in requests. Review differences in structured output and function-calling events; run the provided smoke tests in redwood-quickstarts to validate behavior before wide rollout.
notes: No customer-facing breaking changes. Be mindful of output differences in deterministic runs; customers should pin model versions when determinism is required. Telemetry will include sanitized metadata for debugging.
